mechanism_narrative: A 2% quarterly increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strengthening economic growth, leading to increased consumer spending and, subsequently, higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in > 50% of quarters with 2%+ GDPC1 growth, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, signaling a tightening monetary cycle, S&P 500 forward returns tend to be negative over the next 20 trading days due to increased borrowing costs.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Jointly, when UNRATE falls below 4% and PAYEMS increases by 200,000+ in a month, signaling a strong labor market, S&P 500 returns tend to be positive over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in > 60% of instances meeting the joint trigger, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 4-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 5% monthly increase in INDPRO, indicating a surge in industrial production, predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in > 50% of months with 5%+ INDPRO growth, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) increases by 1%+ in a month, signaling increased consumer spending, and concurrently HOUST (housing starts) rises by 5%+, indicating a strong housing market, S&P 500 returns tend to be positive over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in > 55% of instances meeting the joint trigger, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 4-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in CPIAUCSL (consumer price index) by 0.5%+ in a month, indicating easing inflation pressures, predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as real interest rates become more favorable.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in > 50% of months with 0.5%+ CPIAUCSL decrease, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always, the direction of PAYEMS (non-farm payroll employment) change predicts the direction of S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as labor market trends reflect overall economic health.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.05 over any 5-year rolling window, or SPX returns contradict PAYEMS direction in > 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of low UNRATE (< 5%), a 1%+ monthly increase in HOUST (housing starts) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as low unemployment amplifies the impact of housing market growth.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in > 60% of instances meeting the trigger, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 4-year rolling window.
